text:
marta: Heads up — customers in eu-west-1 are seeing intermittent failures when talking to our model infra via the VPC endpoint. Health checks for the interface endpoints are flipping to UnHealthy and then back.

lee: Seen this too. Metrics show spike in connection resets from the endpoint ENIs, then NAT gateway capacity kicks in and requests route out different path.

sre-bot: Incident alert: vpce-08c4a9f1 health_check_unhealthy (count=3) — triggered at 2026-03-17T15:12:34Z

ben: Quick checklist: route table associations, security group rules on the ENIs, and target health for the service. Did anyone change the hosted zone or split-horizon DNS recently?

marta: No DNS changes AFAIK. This looks like a mix of SG+route flapping. I found some ENIs in that subnet with no route table explicitly associated (relies on main). Also saw NAT gateway metrics spike at the same time — possible cold-starts causing conn tracking exhaustion?

lee: Putting a couple of commands here I ran:
```
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=network-interface-id,Values=eni-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-endpoint-id,Values=vpce-08c4a9f1
```
Output showed ENI attachments shifting between subnets (weird) and one endpoint with SecurityGroupIds: [sg-0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e] that doesn't allow ephemeral ports from our infra subnets.

raj: I ran a dig against the private hosted zone and got split responses depending on which AZ I hit: sometimes returns interface endpoint IP, sometimes regional NLB ip in another account. Suspect Route 53 policy + failover is resolving to a non-VPC variant occasionally.

ben: If the endpoint DNS alternates between interface ENI IPs and cross-account NLB, health checks could be hitting wrong targets. Let's confirm the endpoint is configured with private DNS enabled and the hosted zone assoc is only the customer VPCs.

marta: Confirmed privateDnsEnabled = true for the VPC endpoint, but there's also a legacy public alias record in that hosted zone for the same name (created by old onboarding script). Looks like sometimes the resolver path returns the alias.

lee: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) remove the legacy public alias record, 2) tighten SG on endpoint to allow only our infra subnets, 3) explicitly associate the endpoint with the correct route table(s) in each AZ.

raj: Also add iptables conntrack tuning on the NAT instances / check TGW NAT throughput if used. Cold starts on managed NAT can spike ephemeral usage.

marta: I'll remove the alias after approval. Ben can you confirm there's no external dependency on that public record?

ben: I'll audit DNS change history and call out any customers using the public name. If none, we can delete.

lee: After removing alias, we should monitor for at least 30m and watch vpce health + connect resets. Also consider enabling endpoint private DNS logging for a while.

marta: Taking action: 1) open PR to remove alias (link: https://git.redwood/repo/dns/changes/234) 2) creating runbook task to attach route tables to each AZ-specific subnet for the endpoint 3) tightening SG to allow 10.0.0.0/8 (our infra) only.

sre-bot: Runbook automation: endpoint-route-assoc job queued for vpce-08c4a9f1 by marta at 2026-03-17T15:28:10Z

raj: If health checks keep flipping after DNS cleanup, let's also look at ENI quotas in that account — running out of ephemeral ENIs can cause the endpoint service to reassign.

marta: Agree. I'll follow up with account quota check and link findings here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lee: I'll keep the alert page open and update once we see stable Healthy state.

ben: FYI — I found one customer using the public name but it's an internal test with no prod traffic. I'll coordinate removal window.

marta: Update: alias removed at 2026-03-17T15:40:02Z. Health check count dropping. Will monitor and close in 1h if stable.

sre-bot: Resolved alert: vpce-08c4a9f1 health_check_unhealthy cleared at 2026-03-17T15:52:17Z
